issues.issue: Missing index on comments.userId prevents efficient retrieval of user comments if needed, and lacks composite index for articleId+createdAt for sorting.
issues.fix: Add index {userId: 1} and {articleId: 1, createdAt: -1} to comments collection.

issues.issue: articles.indexes includes redundant {author.id: 1, createdAt: 1} alongside {authorId: 1, createdAt: 1}.
issues.fix: Remove the redundant index on author.id to reduce write overhead.

issues.issue: favorites and followers use compound _id but lack explicit indexes on individual fields for standalone queries.
issues.fix: Ensure _id subfields are indexed or add separate indexes if queries filter by single field.

self_review_changes: In collection articles: remove the extendedRefs entry "author"; keep the plain field authorId (from userId, type int); remove the index {"author.id":1,"createdAt":1}.
In collection comments: remove the extendedRefs entry "author" and add a plain field authorId (from userId, type int).
In collection articles: remove the counter commentsCount. In collection users: remove the counter followingCount.
Set the articles indexes to exactly: {"slug":1} (NOT unique), {"createdAt":-1}, {"authorId":1,"createdAt":-1}, {"tagList":1,"createdAt":-1}.
Set the comments indexes to exactly: {"articleId":1}.
Set the users indexes to exactly: {"username":1} (NOT unique), {"email":1} (NOT unique). The original database has no unique constraints and the API behavior must not change.
